content:
jonah: Quick thought — we should start a concrete plan to harmonize the orchestration surface between control-plane APIs and runtime route adapters. RFC link: https://redwood/internals/rfcs/orch-surface-v2 :thinking_face:

maria: +1. Can you sketch the problem briefly? I know we've got multiple glue layers now.

jonah: Short version: three teams own overlapping entrypoints (router, policy, rollout). Each exposes slightly different fields and error models. That causes duplicated adapter logic and flaky fallbacks when we failover to cheaper models.

lex: Do you mean unify into a single 'orchestration-adapter' library or standardize the public contract only?

jonah: Prefer a library + small facade. Library for common shapes (route metadata, cost hints, timeout hints), facade per plane to support incremental cutover.

sam: Concern: library vs service — if we push logic to a shared lib, deploy burden shifts to every repo. Service approach centralizes upgrades but adds runtime dependency.

maria: Tradeoffs: library = local control, faster perf; service = single version, easier QoS. We need to decide based on rollout risk and latency budget.

lex: Proposal: do library first but keep compatibility layer in control plane to call remote adapter if needed. That buys safety for heavy-traffic paths.

rana: +1. Also we should add explicit version field to the request envelope now. Backwards compatibility will be easier.

jonah: Agreed. Drafts of action items:
1) spike (2w) to extract common types + validation
2) add envelope v field and adapter negotiation header
3) implement facade in control-plane to translate old->new
4) runtime adopts library at service boundary
5) gradual rollout with A/B and canary

sam: Add perf gating: integration tests with p99 latency < current + 10ms.

eng-sre-bot: Reminder: open an infra runbook for rollback and disk usage if adapters add caching.

maria: Who owns the spike?

lex: I can lead the spike with help from sam for perf and rana for compat tests.

jonah: Lex, can you open a short ADR summarizing choices and put tasks into the 'modularization' epic? Ping @eng-sre for rollout window.

lex: Will do. I'll post the ADR draft tomorrow and tag this thread. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — this feels actionable. Keep it small and measurable.

jonah: Cool — let's land the spike plan in the next sprint. Closing for now.
